text: Julia died of pure fear and nervous shock.
The 'speckled band' Julia named meant the gypsies, perhaps their spotted handkerchiefs.
The gypsies in the plantation had a hand in Julia's death.
A low whistle and a metallic clang sounded just before Julia came out of her room.
A low whistle sounded in Julia's old room the night before the visit.
Nothing and no one could have got into Julia's room from outside, and the rooms have no communication with each other.
Roylott made the marks on Helen's wrist.
Helen came by dog-cart (seated on the driver's left) and the first train.
The man she looks to for help (named only later, Armitage) takes Helen's fears for a nervous woman's fancies.
Roylott traced his stepdaughter to Baker Street.
There is a ventilator joining Julia's room to Roylott's.
The metallic clang Helen heard was one of the metal bars of the shutters falling back into place.
